Carriers operating in the Portland-Vancouver area object to the application of the proposed population-mileage formula to these cities because it will bring each city into the commercial zone of the other and thereby exempt traffic moving between these cities from economic regulation. At the present time each of these cities has a separate specifically defined commercial zone. Carriers presently handling traffic moving between these two cities fear it will be diverted by unregulated carriers if the proposal is adopted.
Arguments favoring zone expansion by shippers, local interests, State agencies, and individuals. - The Interim Report stated that the overwhelming majority of these parties favored some type of zone expansion. This fact was reinforced by the representations of these interests which were filed in response to the Interim Report. Of the 121 shipper and local interest representatives, 120 favor and one opposes expansion. All three State agencies support expansion. The individuals who filed representations, most of whom are employees of regulated motor carriers, oppose the propose 143 to 1.
Those interests who favor zone and terminal area expansion argue generally that commercial zones must be expanded to encompass industrial parks, shopping centers, and other business establishments which are closely connected
Of the 124 shipper and local interest representations filed in response to the rulemaking notice, 116 favored and 8 opposed expansion. Two State agencies favored the proposal and one opposed it. Three individuals favored expansion and three opposed it.
